newsitem.title: USA: Sport Supply says violated loan covenant.
newsitem.headline: Sport Supply says violated loan covenant.

text.p: Sport Supply Group Inc said on Monday it would have to borrow at higher interest rates because it violated a single earnings related covenant in its loan agreement.

The size and availability of the credit line had not changed but the company said in a statement it would have to borrow at higher rates until it cured the default through debt reduction or higher earnings.
Sport Supply said it had $26 million in outstanding debt under its $50 million credit line.
The outstanding loan balance had been reclassified as a liability, it said.

Sport Supply also said it had a goal of eliminating all outstanding bank debt through the combination of security and asset sales. It said it was continuing to negotiate with its senior lender to amend the credit facility and provide additional borrowing capacity.
It said in a statement it expected its financial restructuring to be completed by the October 31 fiscal year end.
Earlier the company third quarter earnings of $0.06 per share, before a $0.55 per share charge associated with the planned disposal of remaining golf assets.
